answers.explanation: Deciding what to move into and out of memory is memory management.
Creating and deleting processes is process management.
Primitives to manipulate files and directories belong to file-system management.
Spooling is part of the I/O subsystem's memory management of I/O.
Deadlock handling is one of the five process-management activities.
Tracking memory use is memory management. Tracking free DISK blocks is mass-storage management.
Cache coherency keeps every CPU's cache up to date.
